content: 1. An applicant who satisfies the minimum admission requirements for a specific program is eligible for consideration. The number of available spots reflects the capacity of the educational and training institution and its programs. 2. Health workforce education and training programs are structured sequences of educational activities designed to achieve specific learning objectives or tasks over a sustained period. These programs aim to enhance health-related knowledge, skills, and competencies, and to train new health workers. 3. Many health workforce education and training programs have a numerus clausus, which limits the number of available spots for a given program. 4. Health workforce planning involves strategies to ensure the adequate supply and distribution of health workers in alignment with policy objectives and the demand for health labor. 5. Higher education encompasses all forms of post-secondary studies, training, or research provided by universities or other institutions recognized as higher education establishments by the relevant state authorities. 6. Hospital patient bed-days refer to the time a patient spends confined to a hospital bed overnight. Day cases, where patients are admitted and discharged on the same day, are excluded. 7. Human resources for health include all individuals engaged in activities primarily aimed at improving health. This workforce can be categorized into three groups: those with health vocational training working in health services, those without formal health training working in health services, and those with health training working outside the health sector or not currently active in the labor market. 8. Inpatient visits are consultations or treatments in a hospital that require the patient to stay overnight. 9. In-service training refers to training received while employed in the health sector. It focuses on maintaining core competencies and developing new skills in response to public health needs and consumer demand. 10. The institutional sector includes government units, non-profit institutions serving households, non-financial corporations, and households, as defined by the System of National Accounts. 11. The International Health Regulations (2005) is a legally binding agreement among 196 countries, including all WHO member states, aimed at preventing and responding to acute public health risks that could cross borders and threaten global populations. 12. Interprofessional education occurs when two or more health professionals learn together to foster effective collaboration and improve health outcomes. The term professional includes individuals with the knowledge or skills to contribute to the physical, mental, and social well-being of a community. 13. A job vacancy refers to a paid position that is newly created, unoccupied, or about to become vacant, for which the employer is actively seeking a suitable candidate from outside the organization. 14. Leave entitlements to care for sick family members allow employees to take time off, sometimes paid, to care for a child, partner, parent, or other family member in need due to illness. 15. Licensure is the process of granting a permit or mandatory certification to practice in a specific health field, issued by a legitimate regulatory body. 16. Lifelong learning includes all forms of education, training, and informal learning undertaken throughout life to improve knowledge, skills, and competencies, including professional ethics. 17. Lifelong learning systems integrate schools, colleges, universities, community-based learning facilities, and health workplaces into learning networks that promote equality of opportunity, gender equality, and social inclusion. 18. Maternity leave is employment-protected leave for women around the time of childbirth or adoption, with a minimum period of 14 weeks as stipulated by the ILO convention. 19. Generalist medical doctors diagnose, treat, and prevent illnesses and maintain general health using modern medical principles. They provide comprehensive care and may oversee treatment plans implemented by other healthcare providers. 20. Specialist medical doctors focus on specific diseases, patient types, or treatment methods. They use advanced diagnostic and therapeutic techniques and may engage in medical education and research. 21. Gynecologists specialize in women's health, particularly the reproductive system. Obstetricians focus on pregnancy and childbirth. Pediatricians specialize in the health and development of children. 22. Midwives provide and evaluate care services before, during, and after pregnancy and childbirth. 23. Net inflow refers to the difference between the number of health workers entering and leaving the health labor market in a given year. Net outflow occurs when more workers leave than enter. 24. A newly active health worker is one who begins practicing in a specific profession during a given year. 25. Nurse practitioners are advanced practice nurses with expert knowledge, complex decision-making skills, and clinical competencies for expanded practice. A master’s degree is recommended for entry-level practice. 26. Nursing professionals provide care for individuals who are physically or mentally ill, elderly, injured, or disabled. 27. An occupation is defined as a set of jobs with similar tasks and duties. A job refers to tasks performed by one person, either for an employer or in self-employment. 28. Occupational health and safety is the science of identifying, evaluating, and controlling workplace hazards that could harm workers' health and well-being, considering the impact on surrounding communities and the environment. 29. Official development assistance refers to financial flows aimed at promoting economic development and welfare in developing countries, provided by donor government agencies. 30. Parental leave is employment-protected leave for parents, often supplementary to maternity and paternity leave, and may follow maternity leave in some countries. 31. Part-time employment refers to individuals working less than 30 hours per week in their main job. 32. Paternity leave is employment-protected leave for fathers around the time of childbirth. 33. People-centered care adopts the perspectives of individuals, families, and communities as active participants in health systems. It emphasizes education and support for individuals to make decisions and participate in their care. 34. Primary care teams consist of professionals with complementary roles in patient care, fostering mutual respect, shared responsibility, and cooperation. 35. The primary object of attack includes individuals, infrastructure, vehicles, and other health-related items subjected to violence or obstruction. 36. Public expenditure refers to spending from public funds, including investments in facilities and capital transfers to the private sector for construction and equipment. 37. The public health workforce is responsible for core public health activities such as disease surveillance, health assessments, and emergency preparedness. 38. Qualified educators meet the minimum academic qualifications required to teach a subject at the relevant level in a given country. 39. Registered health workers are those listed in a health workforce registry, regardless of their activity or license validity. 40. Relicensure involves recertifying a health worker to meet the standards required for practicing a specific occupation.
